chunks: And from him, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the one who accuses the foundling.
He (peace be upon him) said: "The accuser of the foundling is flogged, and the accuser of the son of al-la'nah is flogged."

key_terms.ابْنُ اللَّعْنَةِ: Son of al-la'nah (child of the mutual curse ritual in divorce)
key_terms.قَاذِف: Accuser (one who makes a formal accusation of zina)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for accusing a foundling child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that the accuser of a foundling (laqit) receives the hadd punishment, explicitly equating this case with that of the 'son of al-la'nah' (the child of khula' or mutual curse). This parallel underscores the jurisprudential consistency in applying the same penal measure to accusations regarding lineage in distinct but related contexts of family law. The ruling highlights the importance of verifying lineage claims to preserve social and legal integrity within the Shia fiqh framework.
